title: Station Feed and Line Patrol Report: Circuits 6, 7, 11, 12

fields.organization: Foothills Electric Cooperative — System Meteorology & Line Patrol
fields.formTitle: Field Conditions Report — Fire Weather Watch Circuits
fields.location: Circuit 6 Coyote Ridge weather station; Circuit 11 Gulch Saddle weather station; Circuit 7 and Circuit 12 rights-of-way; Circuit 12 right-of-way above Kestrel Springs
fields.inspector: Dale Ostrowski, Line Patrol Supervisor (field report by phone); station data compiled by M. Halvorsen, System Meteorologist
fields.weather: Clear and dark, 41°F, RH 17%, wind W 22 mph gusting 38 mph at Coyote Ridge
fields.summary: At 05:15 MDT the co-op station feed shows Coyote Ridge (Circuit 6) at a 38 mph gust and 22 mph sustained, and Gulch Saddle (Circuit 11) at a 37 mph gust and 21 mph sustained. Both are still below the 45 mph gust / 25 mph sustained trigger. Model guidance puts gusts at 45–52 mph at both stations by 09:00. Line Patrol reports that fuel sticks on Circuits 7 and 12 read 7 percent. The Circuit 12 right-of-way above Kestrel Springs cannot be reached by bucket truck in the present wind. Supervisor Ostrowski states: "Once the gusts hit we can't patrol or clear that line. Do you want my crews staged or sent home? I need an answer by six."

findings.notes: 05:15 gust 38 mph, sustained 22 mph. Rising since 05:00. Below trigger.
05:15 gust 37 mph, sustained 21 mph. Below trigger.
Gusts forecast at 45–52 mph at both stations. Consistent with the NWS Red Flag Warning issued at 347 AM, with timing ±1 hour.

findings.item: Circuit 12 right-of-way access above Kestrel Springs
findings.notes: Bucket Truck 31 cannot safely climb the right-of-way in the current wind. The line cannot be patrolled or cleared once the gusts arrive.
Not patrolled this morning. Crews are holding at the Pine Gulch yard.

actionsTaken: 05:08 Fuel sticks read on the Circuit 7 and Circuit 12 rights-of-way
05:11 Bucket Truck 31 turned back on the Circuit 12 right-of-way above Kestrel Springs
05:15 Station feed pulled for Coyote Ridge and Gulch Saddle and checked against model guidance
05:16 Supervisor Ostrowski phoned the Operations Director
Line Patrol Crews 1–3 holding at the Pine Gulch yard until further direction
recommendations: Operations Director to direct by 06:00 whether line crews are staged or released
If crews are staged, assign them to the Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 patrol routes so re-energization patrols can start in daylight
Continue station polling every 15 minutes and alert at any gust of 45 mph or more, or any sustained wind of 25 mph or more
fields.photosNote: 3 attachments: FEC_STN_0540.csv (Coyote Ridge and Gulch Saddle 10-minute data, 05:00–05:15); IMG_2214 (fuel stick reading, Circuit 12); IMG_2215 (Bucket Truck 31 turned back on the Circuit 12 right-of-way, taken in the dark with a flash)
fields.signature: Dale Ostrowski, Line Patrol Supervisor, Foothills Electric Cooperative

instructorNote: This is a clue inject. Every de-energization criterion in co-op plan section 3 is now met or forecast to be met (Red Flag Warning, gusts of 45 mph or more forecast, fuel at 7 percent, Circuit 12 cannot be patrolled), even though the gusts measured now are below the trigger. Check that OPS makes and logs the Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 decision by 06:00 on these thresholds and stages the crews for re-energization patrols instead of sending them home.
